cues: Mashed ripe flesh can replace some oil in muffins, keeping their crumb moist after baking.
A little sweetness from the soft fruit can balance tart berries in a homemade breakfast bowl.
A spoonful of mashed fruit can mellow unsweetened cocoa, balancing bitterness in a quick dessert.
Mashed pulp can bind oat clusters during baking, helping homemade granola form crisp, shareable pieces.
A ripe portion stirred into plain kefir adds gentle sweetness without relying on syrups or packaged flavorings.
Its mild aroma can make homemade custard taste sweeter, even when the recipe uses little added sugar.
